defaults.permitted_development: Across West Sussex, a side extension normally only falls within Class A if it is single storey, stays behind the principal elevation and does not exceed half the width of the original house. Width, parking loss and the effect of the flank wall usually decide whether it still reads as a modest addition.

rules.height_rules: Across West Sussex, the usual side-extension fallback is an overall height of up to 4m, with eaves at or below 3m where any part sits within 2m of a boundary. Keeping the side roof low is usually what stops the flank wall becoming visually heavy.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate side-extension depth allowance in the way people often expect. The real test is whether the addition stays clearly subordinate to the original house and does not turn the side elevation into an oversized new wing.
rules.boundary_rules: Across West Sussex, the key boundary checks are width, side-gap character, neighbour outlook and whether the addition creates an overbearing flank wall from the street or adjoining land.
rules.roof_rules: Keep the roof clearly secondary to the main house. A simple, low side roof is usually easier to defend than a taller form that competes with the original ridgeline.
rules.materials_rules: Materials should match or sit very closely with the existing house so the side addition reads as part of the dwelling rather than a bolt-on block.

rules.permitted_development: The usual side-extension fallback is still Class A, but only where the addition is single storey, behind the main front wall and no more than half the width of the original house. In Adur, side work on visible or corner plots tends to be judged hard because the addition is part of the public street scene, not just a private side gap.

rules.height_rules: Height is usually straightforward on paper: up to 4m overall, and no more than 3m to the eaves where the extension sits close to the boundary. In Adur, exposed side elevations carry longer public views, so roof pitch and apparent shoulder height matter just as much as the measured maximum.
rules.depth_rules: Depth is judged less by a fixed metre rule than by whether the extension remains clearly subsidiary to the original side wall and does not read as an overlarge flank addition.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary issues for a side extension usually come down to side-gap character, neighbour outlook and whether the new wall reads as a hard edge on the plot. In Adur, even where neighbour distance is acceptable, a side extension can still fail the boundary test if it closes down an open, visible edge.
rules.roof_rules: The roof should stay subordinate to the house and avoid creating a bulky flank mass. On taller side work, matching roof pitch and keeping the addition back from the front are usually critical design points.
rules.materials_rules: Use materials that tie the extension back to the original house, especially on prominent flank walls that are visible from the street. On exposed coastal sites, roof profile, external finish and visual impact can carry more weight than on a routine suburban plot.

restrictions.conservation_area: Conservation area status usually makes visible side work more sensitive, especially where openness between buildings forms part of local character.
restrictions.listed_building: If the house is listed, side work should be treated as a heritage proposal first, not as routine permitted development.
restrictions.article4_notes: Do not assume the Class A fallback is universal: an Article 4 direction can still disapply it for the exact property or street.
